stem: Which two biological ingredients does the model combine to form and combine overlapping neuronal assemblies?
choices: Neuromodulatory gating and spike-timing-dependent plasticity
Short-term synaptic plasticity and feedback connections
Separate error units and global teaching signals
Nonlinear dendritic branches and distinct inhibitory populations
answer: Nonlinear dendritic branches and distinct inhibitory populations
label: Summary · the two ingredients

stem: At what spatial scale is synaptic plasticity gated so that one neuron can belong to several assemblies without overwriting?
choices: The whole neuron
The local inhibitory population
The individual dendrite
The cortical area
answer: The individual dendrite
label: Summary · why no overwriting

stem: How was each excitatory neuron modelled in the spiking network?
choices: A leaky-integrate-and-fire soma with several dendrites
A single-compartment leaky-integrate-and-fire unit
A Hodgkin-Huxley soma with passive dendritic cables
A rate unit with a saturating nonlinearity
answer: A leaky-integrate-and-fire soma with several dendrites
label: Results · neuron model

stem: Which receptor type supplied the nonlinear component of dendritic integration in the model?
choices: AMPA channels
NMDA channels
GABA-A channels
Voltage-gated sodium channels
answer: NMDA channels
label: Results · which channel is nonlinear

stem: What could sufficiently strong inhibition do to the local dendritic NMDA spikes that strong excitation evoked?
choices: Shorten them to under a millisecond
Convert them into somatic action potentials
Prevent them entirely
Spread them to neighbouring branches
answer: Prevent them entirely
label: Results · NMDA spikes

stem: What quantity determined whether a synapse was potentiated or depressed in the model's plasticity rule?
choices: Somatic firing rate against a single threshold
The timing of pre- and postsynaptic spikes
Filtered dendritic voltage against two thresholds
The calcium concentration at the synapse
answer: Filtered dendritic voltage against two thresholds
label: Results · plasticity rule

stem: What sequence of plasticity regimes did a dendrite pass through as its active excitatory input fell or its inhibition rose?
choices: Potentiation, then depression, then none
Depression, then potentiation, then none
None, then depression, then potentiation
Potentiation, then none, then depression
answer: Potentiation, then depression, then none
label: Results · plasticity regimes

stem: What happened to the plasticity-regime switch when NMDA synapses were made linear in a control simulation?
choices: It needed far larger input changes to shift
It disappeared altogether at every input level
It shifted toward depression at all input levels
It became faster but less reliable
answer: It needed far larger input changes to shift
label: Results · why nonlinearity matters

stem: How did activity and plasticity on one dendritic branch relate to the other branches of the same neuron?
choices: Strongly coupled through the soma
Largely isolated from them
Coupled only when an NMDA spike occurred
Averaged across branches before plasticity
answer: Largely isolated from them
label: Results · branch independence

stem: With a context switched off, what was the state of the matching inhibitory input and the synapses on its dendrite?
choices: Inhibition silent, so no plasticity on that dendrite
Inhibition active, so depression on that dendrite
Inhibition silent, so potentiation on that dendrite
Inhibition active, so no plasticity on that dendrite
answer: Inhibition active, so no plasticity on that dendrite
label: Results · what off means

stem: In the model's baseline state, with every context off, what was happening to plasticity across the network?
choices: It was suppressed by highly active inhibition
It proceeded slowly across all dendrites
It was restricted to feedforward synapses
It depressed every recurrent synapse
answer: It was suppressed by highly active inhibition
label: Results · baseline state

stem: What happened on a dendrite that received many strong excitatory inputs while its context signal stayed off?
choices: Potentiation occurred, but more slowly
No plasticity occurred there at all
Depression occurred instead of potentiation
Plasticity spread to the neuron's other dendrites
answer: No plasticity occurred there at all
label: Results · the veto

stem: How many multi-compartment excitatory neurons made up the recurrent network used to study assembly formation?
choices: 400 neurons
40 neurons
4,000 neurons
20 neurons
answer: 400 neurons
label: Results · network size

stem: What kept assembly size roughly constant as assemblies formed in the recurrent network?
choices: Inhibition plus dendrite-specific normalization
A hard cap on the number of plastic synapses
Synaptic scaling at the somatic compartment
Decay of unused recurrent weights over time
answer: Inhibition plus dendrite-specific normalization
label: Results · assembly size control

stem: What fraction of recurrent neurons ended up in some assembly after twenty were imprinted in one context?
choices: About 25%
About 50%
About 75%
Nearly all of them
answer: About 75%
label: Results · storage capacity

stem: Which assemblies did the random-connectivity statistics predict would end up smaller?
choices: Those imprinted later
Those imprinted in a switched context
Those imprinted earlier
Those driven by the fewest input neurons
answer: Those imprinted earlier
label: Results · why order matters

stem: How did recall of early-imprinted assemblies compare with later ones after all twenty were learned?
choices: Stronger, because they were consolidated longest
Weaker, and indistinguishable from background
Weaker, but still above background
Identical, since assembly size was held constant
answer: Weaker, but still above background
label: Results · recall by order

stem: What happened when assemblies learned in one context were probed with their own inputs in a different context?
choices: They were reactivated at a slightly lower rate
They were not reactivated
They were reactivated but with different neurons
They were depressed by the mismatched context
answer: They were not reactivated
label: Results · context-dependent recall

stem: How much of the original input was needed to reactivate a whole assembly in the context where it was learned?
choices: Fewer than half the input neurons
Nearly all the input neurons
About three-quarters of the input neurons
A single input neuron
answer: Fewer than half the input neurons
label: Results · pattern completion

stem: Besides reducing how many inputs were active, what other weakening of the input still produced pattern completion?
choices: Delaying the input by several hundred milliseconds
Presenting the inputs in a scrambled order
Lowering the input firing rate
Removing the contextual signal
answer: Lowering the input firing rate
label: Results · weak-input completion

stem: What did the single-dendrite control model show that multiple dendritic branches are not required for?
choices: Assembly learning within a single context
Pattern completion from partial input
Keeping assembly size constant
Recall above background firing
answer: Assembly learning within a single context
label: Results · what dendrites add

stem: What share of input neurons did each newly imprinted assembly share with the original assembly in the interference test?
label: Results · overlap design

stem: What happened to the original assembly's pattern completion as overlapping assemblies were added in the same context?
choices: It was unaffected throughout
It deteriorated, leaving a small responsive core
It vanished completely to background
It improved as recurrent weights grew
answer: It deteriorated, leaving a small responsive core
label: Results · same-context interference

stem: What restored the original assembly's pattern completion despite overlapping assemblies being added?
choices: Lowering the input rate for new assemblies
Reducing the overlap below 25%
Switching context between sets of new assemblies
Adding feedforward inhibition to new assemblies
answer: Switching context between sets of new assemblies
label: Results · context switch rescues

stem: How was forgetting of the original assembly quantified in this model?
choices: Neurons that dropped out of the assembly
The decline in recall firing rate over time
The number of new assemblies that could be added
Within-assembly synapses that underwent depression
answer: Within-assembly synapses that underwent depression
label: Results · measuring forgetting

stem: What mapping between contexts, inhibitory subgroups and dendrites does the model assume?
choices: One subgroup per context, all dendrites of a neuron
All subgroups per context, one dendrite per neuron
Random assignment of subgroups to dendrites
One subgroup per context, one dendrite per neuron
answer: One subgroup per context, one dendrite per neuron
label: Results · key assumption

stem: What did randomizing the wiring from contexts to inhibitory neurons, or inhibitory neurons to dendrites, do to stored assemblies?
choices: They were preserved as well as under one-to-one wiring
They were substantially modified despite context switching
They failed to form in the first place
They became larger but remained stable
answer: They were substantially modified despite context switching
label: Results · relaxing the assumption

stem: What did the authors propose could make the required one-to-one gating wiring emerge rather than be assumed?
choices: Genetically specified interneuron subtypes
Pruning of excess dendritic branches
Homeostatic scaling of inhibitory synapses
Winner-take-all plasticity on inhibitory connections
answer: Winner-take-all plasticity on inhibitory connections
label: Results · where the wiring comes from

stem: What connectivity between areas did the multi-area simulations deliberately omit?
choices: Recurrent connections within each area
Feedforward inhibition between areas
Contextual input to downstream areas
Reciprocal feedback connections
answer: Reciprocal feedback connections
label: Results · multi-area architecture

stem: What did activating the same area X neurons in a second context do downstream in area Y?
choices: Recruited the same area Y neurons as before
Failed to activate any area Y neurons
Depressed the assembly learned in the first context
Recruited a different subset of area Y neurons
answer: Recruited a different subset of area Y neurons
label: Results · same input, new context

stem: What did selecting area X neurons that targeted newly gated dendrites of the original assembly's neurons produce?
choices: A new assembly of entirely different neurons
A new assembly of largely the same neurons
Reactivation of the original assembly without learning
Depression of the original assembly's weights
answer: A new assembly of largely the same neurons
label: Results · same neurons, new dendrites

stem: Why were the digits 0 and 1 paired with the letters O and l in the association task?
choices: They sound alike but look entirely different
They are the most frequent characters in the dataset
They activate non-overlapping visual assemblies
They look alike but sound entirely different
answer: They look alike but sound entirely different
label: Results · task stimuli

stem: What did the two contexts in the concept area represent during the visual-auditory task?
choices: Whether the stimulus was round or vertical
Whether the stimulus was a letter or a number
Whether the stimulus was seen or heard
Whether the stimulus was novel or familiar
answer: Whether the stimulus was a letter or a number
label: Results · what the context was

stem: Where did representations of visually similar stimuli become non-overlapping?
choices: In the visual area, not the concept area
In the concept area, not the visual area
In the auditory area, not the concept area
In all three areas equally
answer: In the concept area, not the visual area
label: Results · where separation happens

stem: Tested with a visual image not used in training, how did the downstream visual area perform on the similar pairs?
choices: It distinguished them as well as the concept area
It failed to distinguish them
It distinguished them only with auditory input
It responded only to the digits, not the letters
answer: It failed to distinguish them
label: Results · test on new images

stem: What happened in the concept area when only the visual half of a learned audiovisual pair was presented?
choices: Only the directly driven neurons responded
The assembly was suppressed by the missing input
Recurrence amplified it into most of the assembly
A different context's assembly activated instead
answer: Recurrence amplified it into most of the assembly
label: Results · half the input

stem: What happened when the contexts were redefined by visual shape, grouping the round characters together and the vertical ones together?
choices: The concept area no longer separated similar stimuli
The concept area separated them even better
The visual area separated them instead
Assemblies failed to form in any area
answer: The concept area no longer separated similar stimuli
label: Results · when context fails

stem: After silencing half of a middle area's assembly neurons, what happened to the assembly two areas downstream?
choices: Its activity fell by about half as well
It fell to background activity
It remained highly active
It activated a different set of neurons
answer: It remained highly active
label: Results · upstream damage

stem: What did the strong recurrent within-assembly weights amount to as signals passed through the area hierarchy?
choices: A progressive loss of signal at each stage
A winner-take-all competition between areas
A chain of activity amplification
A delay line encoding stimulus order
answer: A chain of activity amplification
label: Results · amplification chain

stem: How many highly active upstream inputs did a neuron need to join a projection assembly?
choices: At least one
At least four
At least ten
At least twenty
answer: At least four
label: Results · input threshold

stem: How did the neuron identity of simultaneous-association assemblies compare with projection assemblies along the hierarchy?
choices: Increasingly similar in more downstream areas
Identical at every level of the hierarchy
Distinct in the first area but identical later
Increasingly distinct in more downstream areas
answer: Increasingly distinct in more downstream areas
label: Results · association vs projection

stem: What did an association learned on top of an existing projection do to the original assembly's membership?
choices: It replaced most of the original neurons
It retained most of the original neurons
It halved the assembly's membership
It left membership unchanged but weakened weights
answer: It retained most of the original neurons
label: Results · sequential association

stem: In an association built on top of an existing projection, which single input drove the more reliable pattern completion?
choices: The area added later in the association
Either area, equally reliably
Neither area alone, only both together
The area whose projection was learned first
answer: The area whose projection was learned first
label: Results · asymmetric completion

stem: Which interneuron class did the model's feedforward inhibition, stabilizing assembly size against input variation, represent?
choices: Parvalbumin-expressing interneurons
Somatostatin-expressing interneurons
Vasoactive intestinal peptide interneurons
Neurogliaform interneurons
answer: Parvalbumin-expressing interneurons
label: Discussion · two inhibitory roles

stem: How does this model's gating differ from the three-factor learning rules it is compared with?
choices: It is branch-specific rather than whole-neuron
It is neuron-specific rather than population-wide
It uses a global rather than a local signal
It needs no third factor of any kind
answer: It is branch-specific rather than whole-neuron
label: Discussion · versus three-factor rules

stem: How did the authors interpret the contextual signal in their framework?
choices: A simplified top-down signal licensing plasticity
A bottom-up measure of stimulus salience
A neuromodulatory reward prediction error
A homeostatic set point for firing rate
answer: A simplified top-down signal licensing plasticity
label: Discussion · what context is
